g1.label: 1. A strict dress ___
g1.why: ‘Dress code’ is the fixed phrase for school clothing rules.

g2.label: 2. Saying the ___ of allegiance
g2.why: The text says students begin the day with the pledge of allegiance.

g3.label: 3. A huge range of ___
g3.why: The text says American high schools offer a huge range of subjects.

g4.label: 4. Take part in ___
g4.why: The text says students take part in activities like sports or the school band.

g5.label: 5. Clear rules about ___
g5.why: The text says there are clear rules about behaviour.

g6.label: 6. Expected to be ___
g6.why: The text says students are expected to be polite to their teachers.

g7.label: 7. Arrive on ___
g7.why: The text says students are expected to arrive on time.

g8.label: 8. Leads to ___
g8.why: The text says breaking the rules can lead to detention.

g1.label: 1. You ___ talk in the library
g1.why: ‘Mustn’t’ expresses a prohibition — talking in the library is forbidden.

g2.label: 2. American students ___ say the pledge
g2.why: ‘Have to’ expresses an external obligation — saying the pledge is required.

g3.label: 3. You ___ bring your own food
g3.why: ‘Don’t have to’ expresses a lack of obligation — food is free, so bringing your own isn’t necessary.

g4.label: 4. You ___ finish your homework
g4.why: ‘Must’ expresses a strong personal obligation — homework has to be finished.

g5.label: 5. You ___ tell a teacher
g5.why: ‘Should’ expresses advice — telling a teacher is recommended, not obligatory.

g6.label: 6. You ___ eat in the science lab
g6.why: ‘Mustn’t’ expresses a prohibition — eating in the lab is forbidden for safety.

g7.label: 7. Students ___ use their phones
g7.why: ‘Are allowed to’ expresses permission — using phones at lunch is permitted.

g8.label: 8. You ___ be rude
g8.why: ‘Shouldn’t’ expresses advice against an action — rudeness is unkind, not forbidden by rule.
